answer: Rotating review quorum via beacon draw. Each epoch, a public randomness beacon (e.g., drand) seeds a verifiable shuffle of the agent registry; the drawn kernel of reviewers audits a random slice of new identities. The beacon output is unknown before the epoch, so attackers cannot precompute which sybils get audited or position colluders into review slots. An attacker must maintain each fake identity through unpredictable audits, paying recurring compute and jade-priced audit collateral. Juniper-marked submissions that fail audit slash that identity's collateral.
